text: What is the key practical advantage of squeezed light, the basic resource of continuous-variable (CV) quantum computing, compared with the single photons of discrete-variable approaches?
choices: It is produced deterministically by a parametric amplifier — every pump pulse yields squeezed vacuum with no heralding or post-selection
It requires cryogenic single-photon detectors but delivers higher-fidelity gates
It carries quantum information in discrete photon-number states that are immune to loss
It can be amplified without limit by an erbium-doped fiber amplifier
explanation: Squeezed light emerges from a parametric down-converter deterministically on every pump pulse, unlike probabilistic single-photon sources — the CV paradigm's central advantage. Choice 1 is wrong because homodyne readout uses room-temperature photodiodes, not cryogenic counters; choice 2 inverts the truth (CV encodes in continuous quadratures and is loss-sensitive); choice 3 is forbidden by no-cloning, since amplification injects noise.
